emma: Heads-up — after yesterday's tokenizer v2 rollout we saw a ~14% drop in prefix-cache hit rate during peak. Repro + quick notes below.

emma: TL;DR: tokenizer change affected punctuation tokenization and a small fraction of tool-call field serialization, so cache keys diverged. Suspect two good mitigation paths: (A) add tokenizer_version to cache key, (B) do aggressive prompt normalization + toolfield canonical ordering and keep key stable.

emma: Repro steps: run same request before/after tokenizer change. Example diff: 
```
before key: prompt="Order: 1) foo; 2) bar"
after key: prompt="Order: 1) foo ; 2 ) bar"
```
(seen extra spaces and different token boundaries in a few edge cases)

raj: Oof. If we just add `tokenizer_version` to the key we avoid silent collisions but we'll blow away existing cache for that model/version combo. Backfill/warmup required. Tradeoff: correctness vs churn.

lucy: ran a small backfill prototype last night: `python tools/warmup.py --cohort=100k --model=redwood/gpt-small --mode=prefix-only`
Result: hit-rate recovered from ~78% -> ~96% after ~6h of gradual traffic replay. Cost ~= 0.8 GPU-hours (mixed spot + reserved).

lucy: Notes: we had to throttle concurrency to avoid kernel switching thrash — prefill long prefixes caused kernel to switch to long-seq path and latency spiked.

tom: +1 on throttling. Kernel selection heuristic picks different CUDA kernels for >512 tokens; our warmup runner was replaying a lot of long prompts which forced different kernel paths and inflated tail latency. Suggest warmup shape match production token-length distribution and limit parallelism.

emma: Proposed immediate plan:
- short term: deploy a normalization layer that removes incidental whitespace/punct differences and applies canonical ordering to tool/function call fields (stable cheap win).
- medium term: add `tokenizer_version` to cache key but gated behind an opt-in / warmup flag so we can do controlled backfill.
- instrumentation: add histogram of token-length-per-key and per-key hit-rate; surface in Console.

raj: Will draft PR for key schema change. Plan: new key schema = `join([model, prompt_normalized_hash, tool_meta_hash, tokenizer_version?])` where tokenizer_version appended only when `key_strategy=versioned`. We can roll via feature-flag and run backfill job for flagged tenants.

emma: For the backfill job we'll need to be careful about kernel routing: `--max-concurrency` and `--seq-percentiles` flags. Lucy, can you add a `--throttle-kernel` heuristic to the warmup tool?

lucy: Yep. I'll add a `--target-p95` knob and a `--concurrency` cap. Also adding an opt to replay sampled kernel distribution: `--kernel-weight-file`.

infra-bot: deploy: redwood-inference/warmup-runner v1.3.2 -> success (2026-03-17T23:12:05Z) :rocket:

ops-bot: metrics: peak hit-rate drop window 23:05-23:40 UTC, cache_miss_rate +14%, avg latency +6% p95 +23%.

tom: One more gotcha: when we backfill we create many new hotkeys which increases memory pressure on KV nodes. Recommend incremental backfill by cohort and an eviction safety valve (e.g., guard that keeps hotset < X% mem).

emma: Agreed. We'll run backfill in cohorts of 50k keys, monitor KV mem and kernel latency. If mem > 75% pause.

raj: I'll add the metric alarms and a runbook entry for emergency pause + rollback.

lucy: Scheduling backfill for Sat 02:00 UTC. I'll attach kernel-shape config and a small diff to warmup tool in the PR.

sarah: Please @ on the PR and ping infra before starting. I'll coordinate support coverage.

emma: Thanks all. Follow-ups: raj -> PR (key-schema + feature-flag), lucy -> warmup knobs + backfill plan, tom -> eviction guard proposal. We'll reconvene after the first cohort. :thumbsup:
